items.title: How a 'loner' went from a life of privilege to Bondi gunman
items.description: Sajid Akram was a man of unusual secrecy — even to his own family. New details uncovered by Background Briefing shed light on his downward spiral into violence.

items.title: Police pulled him over on his farm. He was tasered 30 seconds later
items.description: Disturbing cases of people wrongly tasered by police on their farm and at school has raised questions over whether officers are too reliant on the devices.

items.title: Gas vs beer: How Pocock caused the government a tax headache
items.description: David Pocock was struggling to find cut-through on the issue of gas taxes, but then a question about the beer excise sparked a social media war of words.

items.title: One year into his second term as PM, Albanese says US 'playing a different role'
items.description: Anthony Albanese says the United States is "playing a different role" in the world under President Donald Trump, forcing Australia and allies to adjust how they respond to unexpected conflicts.

items.title: Fiji considers state of emergency after suspected drug kingpin murder in custody
items.description: The suspected murder of a Fijian underworld figure held in military custody has sparked a new chapter in the island nation's wrestle with drug-related crimes, with the police and military combining forces for a highly visible "crackdown".

items.title: How young actor's big break ended in court battle with Hollywood star
items.description: Charlotte MacInnes and Rebel Wilson are locked in a messy defamation battle involving disparaging social media posts, a "Russian oligarch" and sexual harassment accusations.

items.title: Iran's race: Break the US blockade or risk its economic lifeline
items.description: Analysis of how much oil Iran is producing, shipping and having to store shows pressure is mounting on Tehran, but while experts agree the US blockade is effective, there are questions about whether it can really force Iran back to the negotiating table.

items.title: Shift in the Middle East has implications for countries like Australia
items.description: Donald Trump's earlier signalling that he will neither walk away from the war declaring a victory or escalate it, but will try to starve the Iranians out, suggests there is no clear sign of how this war could end.

items.title: The four women who left 'Australia Street' to try and leave Syria
items.description: Four Australian women, their children and grandchildren are stuck in limbo in Syria after leaving a refugee camp for family members of suspected Islamic State fighters. This is what we know about them.

items.title: What is a town camp and what is life like there for Aboriginal people?
items.description: Kumanjayi Little Baby is believed to be taken from her bed in the night while visiting a town camp near Alice Springs with her mother. This is how town camps came to be and what it is like to live in one.

items.title: Piastri qualifies third for Miami sprint, Norris pole
items.description: Lando Norris starts the Miami Grand Prix sprint race on pole position, with world championship leader Kimi Antonelli denying Oscar Piastri a spot on the front row of the grid.

items.title: What happens when you swap a selfie for a canvas?
items.description: What began as an awkward pose for the Archibald Prize became a meditation on why portrait painting still matters in the age of the iPhone.

items.title: Why many Australians are heading for this island in East Asia
items.description: Lots of Australians travel to Taiwan chasing flavour and wanting to try the best beef noodle soup — but they leave wanting to explore more of its history and nature.

items.title: The alternative classroom disengaged students are choosing to be in
items.description: Of the students who have attended the Alternative Suspension program, 67 per cent have received no further suspensions.

items.title: 1976 in music: The big albums turning 50 this year
items.description: The music industry is always in a state of flux, but what was happening in 1976 was akin to the dinosaurs looking up and seeing a meteor on the way.

items.title: Four for the weekend: Apex, Margo's Got Money Troubles and massaman curry
items.description: What to watch, read, listen to and eat this weekend, according to our culture and food teams.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of an iconic album, a shredding Banksy and that creepy dancing baby gif
items.description: Every question has only two options: one is right, and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: Rare quadruplet birth stuns mum, 45, and doctors
items.description: A Kalgoorlie couple expecting triplets welcome a surprise fourth baby — delivering an extraordinarily rare set of quadruplets that stunned even their doctors.

items.title: Polar blast and snow to follow record May heat over south-east Australia
items.description: Just weeks from winter, and south-east Australia is still enjoying summertime warmth.

items.title: Dingo sightings near primary school put parents on edge
items.description: "Stressed-out" parents are wondering whether to let their children continue to get around unaccompanied, but wildlife advocates say the animals are not as threatening as their reputation suggests.

items.title: Why this cattle farmer is flooding his property with salt water
items.description: More than half a century ago, lush wetlands along the Queensland coastline were cut off from the ocean as farmers built physical barriers to stop salt water flowing into their land. Now, conservation groups and traditional owners are restoring tidal flows and bringing life back to the land.

items.title: Inquiry hears allegations of sabotage and violence on major Brisbane rail project
items.description: Queensland's inquiry into the CFMEU has revealed Cross River Rail was plagued by years of interference. Here are the key takeaways from this week's hearings.

items.title: Spike in number of Tasmanian police on leave due to mental health issues
items.description: More than 100 Tasmanian police officers are currently off duty due to mental health compensation claims, a number that has doubled in five years.

items.title: A guide to the six books vying for the $60,000 Stella Prize
items.description: A memoir by Geraldine Brooks and a historical novel by actor-turned-author Tasma Walton are among the eclectic works up for one of Australia's most prestigious literary awards.

items.title: Melbourne Storm lose seven in a row for the first time in club history
items.description: The Melbourne Storm have sunk to a historic low, losing seven consecutive NRL matches for the first time as the Dolphins powered to victory at a wet Lang Park in Brisbane.
